上原そば.name: Uehara Soba
上原そば.desc: Provisional #5 (13.5/15). An "Okinawa soba and local fish cuisine" shop on high ground with a sweeping view of the sea. Cloudy, MSG-free soup with Agu broth × homemade noodles with whole wheat flour and bonito powder. The bone-in pork ribs on a separate plate and the small dish of local fish sashimi are nice touches.
t: ✨I ate here in February 2025. This time it started with a small mishap 😅 I headed excitedly for "Suba Suba" on Yagaji Island, but it was unexpectedly their regular day off... It had been featured on the local Okinawan TV program "Uchiran", so my expectations were high, and honestly the shock was big. But I switched gears, telling myself that Okinawa soba touring is fun including twists like this, and decided to look for a shop open nearby. That's where I came across "Okinawa Soba and Local Fish Cuisine Uehara Soba" in Yohena, Nago City.
Uehara Soba
Uehara Soba (business hours sign near the entrance outside the shop)

The building's exterior looks like an apartment, so for a moment I felt a little uneasy, wondering if this was really the right place, but a "UEHARA SOBA" sign welcomes you clearly. The sign at the entrance lists the business hours, and there's a homey atmosphere.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance inside
It's a meal ticket machine style with an extensive menu. Besides the standards like hon-soki soba, tebichi soba, and sanmai-niku soba, there's also a sea grape rice bowl on the menu.

When you go inside, the first thing that jumps out at you is the view from the windows. It's on high ground, so the location with a sweeping view of the sea is the best 🌊 It was a bit cloudy that day, but even so the view was plenty refreshing. With wooden tables and calm lighting, it's a stylish, café-like space. It gives the impression of a dining room with a sea view rather than an Okinawa soba shop.
You can see the sea from inside the shop
Inside the shop

This time I ordered the "hon-soki soba". You can choose between rich and light soup, and when I asked the staff, they said "The rich one is ordered a lot". I obediently followed the recommendation and chose rich 😄 The bowl that was brought out has a striking cloudy white soup. Apparently they use Agu broth, and a soft, gentle aroma rises with the steam.
Agu broth, MSG-free, they say
Hon-soki soba (large noodles) ¥1,050

First, a sip of the soup. Smooth and creamy, a perfect balance 😋 It's a different type from Kame Soba's Agu broth, and the flavor reminded me of Getto in Naha City and Tsukikurogi in Uruma City. Delicious 😋
Hon-soki soba (large noodles) ¥1,050

The noodles are homemade, medium-thin and straight, with whole wheat flour and bonito powder kneaded in. These are great too. They have solid chewiness. They go well with the cloudy soup, which clings to them nicely. Personally, these were noodles very much to my liking.

The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), served on a separate plate, look hearty right from the start. When you pick them up with chopsticks there's a bit of a sinewy texture, but in return you can enjoy a properly meaty texture. The seasoning is a little on the sweet side, well soaked in, and simply tasty 😋 Dipping them in the soup gives them yet another character. What made me even happier was the small dish of sashimi. A style you rarely see at other shops, and it shows how much effort they put into local fish cuisine. Sashimi being served at a soba shop is pretty rare, isn't it.

Rating (13.5/15): It was a pinch-hitter shop I went into on short notice, but in the end it was a big hit. Location, soup, noodles, toppings — whichever you look at, the level is high, and honestly I can proudly say it's "recommended-shop level 😄". It's a shop I'd love both tourists and locals to visit at least once. High level. If you like Agu-broth-style Okinawa soba, please give it a try.

上江門そば.name: Uejo Soba
上江門そば.desc: A stamp rally participant with a lovely red-tiled old-house-style building and terrace seats. Its feature is that you can choose the soup from three types: bonito, miso, or soy sauce, and it's equipped with a cashless ticket machine.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some parts added by me 😁
I ate here in October 2024 😆
This time I visited "Uejo Soba" 🍔, which is also a stamp rally participant.
Uejo Soba
When you see the "Uejo" sign along Route 331, turn in from there
Parking lot (it's spacious, so even large crowds are OK 😄)

When I arrived at the shop, the first thing that caught my eye was the spacious parking lot ⛽. A welcome point for customers who come by car 🚗. And then there's the old-house-style building with its striking red-tiled roof 🏡. The interior has a warm wooden feel, the seats are spaciously arranged, and there's a somehow relaxing atmosphere 😌. There are also terrace seats outside, and being able to enjoy a meal while feeling nature on sunny days was appealing too 🌞.
There are outdoor tables, not just indoor seating

Looking at the menu, the "Uejo soba" is set up so you can choose the soup from three types: bonito, miso, or soy sauce 🍲. This is a slightly ramen-like approach, and as a soba lover it struck me as fresh 😊. This time I chose bonito, which is said to be the recommendation 👍. It's a style where you buy a ticket from a ticket machine, and it's perfectly cashless-ready too 💳. Ingenuity typical of an area with many tourists shines through ✨. This time I had the shop's signature item, the "Uejo soba".
A cashless-ready meal ticket machine is nice 👍
Menu
Inside the shop (new and clean)
The "Uejo soba" that was brought out has a look that's simple yet appetizing 🍜. When you take a sip of the soup, a solid bonito broth flavor spreads out 🍼.
Uejo soba (bonito) ¥1,150
Uejo soba (bonito) ¥1,150

The noodles are medium-thick straight noodles with solid chewiness 🍟. They're both chewy and silky smooth, and personally it was a texture I quite liked 😋. The toppings are generous braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs, each well infused with flavor 🍖. The soft-bone pork ribs in particular are simmered tender, with a nice texture that crumbles in your mouth... but it was a little disappointing that both had some sinewiness depending on the cut 🙅‍♀️.
You can also add jushi or small side dishes with the set menu to adjust the volume, which is a nice point 🍳. This time I had just the soba, but next time I come I'd definitely like to try a set 😎.

Looking at it overall — the atmosphere of the whole shop, the many soup options, and service that caters to tourists too — I got the impression that this "Uejo soba" is proposing a new style of Okinawa soba 🌟.
Got Uejo Soba's stamp 👍

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty 🎨 Its coziness and beautiful old-house-style appearance make it worth visiting once 🙌. It was a shop that made me think I might try a different flavor next time 🍲✨. How about everyone giving it a try once?

下地そば.name: Shimoji Soba
下地そば.desc: An old-house diner just like grandma's house from the old days. The ordering system, where you place a magnet on a whiteboard, is fun. The signature Shimoji soba is an everything-on-top bowl with braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, yushi-dofu, and mozuku.
t: I ate here in January 2024. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 33rd of 34 shops 😊 I've steadily eaten my way through the stamp rally and finally made it this far 😆
Shimoji Soba
Shimoji Soba (an old house with a traditional tiled roof 😆)
Entrance
When you go inside, it feels like grandma's house from the old days 😆 So nostalgic lol
Inside the shop (where the family Buddhist altar used to be, there's now a self-service water dispenser 😆)
Inside the shop (Gaggle Sale's autographs are on display)

It was my first time at this shop, so I didn't know the system, but there was no ticket machine, and I had planned to order the "Shimoji soba" featured in the stamp rally booklet anyway, so I said "Shimoji soba, please", and was told, "Put a magnet on number 4 on the whiteboard", so I put a magnet on number 4. The number 4 order on the whiteboard in the photo is mine 😆
It seems the soba menu items are numbered. Maybe the numbers were written on the photo menu posted on the wall, but I didn't notice (^0^;)
They seem to use fresh noodles, and maybe because they take time to boil, I had the impression it took a little while to arrive.
Shimoji soba ¥1,050

As it was also written on the menu on the wall, the "Shimoji soba" is a so-called "everything-on-top" with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu), and mozuku.
The "everything-on-top" menu item reminded me of "Futami Soba" in Nago City, which I introduced in "Holds its own against the recommended ones" 😆
First I taste the soup. Maybe the yushi-dofu broth is mixed in, so the broth base was hard to make out, but it tasted light with a slight pork bone base — rather thin, though.
Shimoji soba ¥1,050

Next I try the noodles. A thin noodle type, and being fresh noodles, they do have a chewy quality. Then I tried the toppings: the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs were on the small side, and their flavor was also thin and light. Including the yushi-dofu and mozuku, it's a light style overall.
Rating (9/15): Ordinary. The building is an old house like an Okinawan grandma's house from the old days, and the atmosphere is very Okinawan, so how about it when you come to this area sightseeing?

与那原家.name: Yonabaru-ya
与那原家.desc: A famous shop along Route 329. Its feature is that you can choose light (bonito flavor) or rich soup, and the rich soup made from pork bones and chicken carcasses comes with gently wavy noodles. Even the regular size includes soft-bone pork ribs, so it's satisfying.
t: I ate here in June 2022 😊
Yonabaru-ya (along Route 329)
Menu
I ordered the "nankotsu soki soba", recommended as the most popular. On top of that, it's a system where you can choose "light" or "rich" soup, and this time I chose the "rich flavor".
The soup, with broth made from pork bones and chicken carcasses, is simply tasty.
Nankotsu soki soba
The noodles are a gently wavy type, and the regular size includes soft-bone pork ribs, so I'm satisfied. The shop is on the large side too.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. This is also a famous shop, so how about trying it once? Next time I'd like to try it with the "light soup, bonito flavor" 😊

並松そば.name: Nanmatsu Soba
並松そば.desc: A shop on high ground between the Kin Town Office and the baseball stadium. The clear soup has an exquisite flavor where you can taste both bonito and pork bone, and the braised pork belly and pork spare ribs toppings come on a separate plate. You can choose thin or flat noodles, and the freedom of 7 size levels plus extra noodles in 100g units is fun too.
t: I ate here in May 2023 😊
Nanmatsu Soba (set back from Route 329)
Menu

I ordered the "Nanmatsu soba", which shares the shop's name. You can choose thin or flat noodles, and when I asked the staff for a recommendation, they recommended "thin noodles", so I chose thin noodles. The sizes were finely divided into 7 levels, from mini to toku-toku-toku-dai (extra-extra-extra large), but this time I ordered the "medium" size 😊
Nanmatsu soba (medium) ¥935

It's called "medium" size, but I thought at other shops it would be in the "large" class. A decent volume. Like a ramen shop, this shop also has a "kaedama" (extra noodles) menu, and it seems you can order in 100g units from 100g (¥110) to 500g (¥550). (I didn't order extra noodles this time)

The soup is a beautiful clear color. I took a sip wondering, "Bonito-based?" I sensed an exquisite flavor where you can taste not just bonito broth but pork bone broth too. Like the "Awase Soba Shokudo" I ate at the other day, I could taste both bonito and pork.
The soy-sauce-based toppings (braised pork belly, pork spare ribs) were on a separate plate, perhaps so their flavor and color wouldn't transfer to the clear color of the soup 😊

The thin noodles are on the soft side. The braised pork belly and pork spare ribs are infused with flavor and tender, and even the soki bones were soft (・・) I don't think I've had soft bones at any other shop so far. Proof of how tenderly they're simmered 😄
Rating (9.5/15): Simply tasty. The soup is a beautiful clear soup, with a flavor where you can taste both bonito and pork, which was nice.

中村商店.name: Nakamura Shoten
中村商店.desc: A shop whose selling point is Agu broth. The Murasho soba, topped with yushi-dofu, pig's feet, braised pork belly, and fish cake, is a very hearty bowl that even comes with a small dish of Agu-broth curry. Set meals with free rice refills too.
t: I went to eat here in March 2023, before surfing (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff point) 😊
Nakamura Shoten
Looking at the menu, it seems Agu is their selling point 😁
Menu
Murasho soba ¥950

Agu broth soup with smooth medium-thick noodles. The toppings — yushi-dofu, pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and fish cake (kamaboko) — make it super hearty (・・) On top of that, it comes with a small dish of curry rice made with Agu broth ^^;
I ordered without looking at the small print on the menu, but it was indeed written there ^^; I thought this wasn't a meal to eat before going into the sea. I'm stuffed.
Rating (9/15): This shop has very hearty menu items, such as champuru dishes and set meals with free rice refills. It's simply tasty 😊, so I recommend it for people who want to eat heartily.
